answer: An island microgrid lets AI agents trade electricity, treating each identity as a vertex that must lock a $100 bond before bidding, whether it supplies a factory or a lantern. Bonds remain locked for 30 days and are slashed for cryptographically provable double-selling. A thousand fake agents therefore require $100,000 in immobilized capital; splitting into more identities creates no free trading capacity and exposes more capital to loss.
